title: Controlled Trial of Budesonide-Formoterol as Needed for Mild Asthma
authors: Beasley R, Holliday M, Reddel HK, Braithwaite I, Ebmeier S, Hancox RJ, et al.
population: Adults aged 18 to 75 years with mild asthma using only a short-acting beta2-agonist; as-needed albuterol 100 µg two inhalations, budesonide 200 µg twice daily plus as-needed albuterol, or as-needed budesonide 200 µg-formoterol 6 µg, open label with electronic inhaler monitoring
funder: Funded by AstraZeneca and the Health Research Council of New Zealand; the registry lists AstraZeneca AB under commercial sector funding and the Medical Research Institute of New Zealand as primary sponsor.
result: 668 of 675 randomised patients were analysed. Annualised exacerbation rate 0.195 with as-needed budesonide-formoterol against 0.400 with as-needed albuterol (relative rate 0.49, 95% CI 0.33 to 0.72) and 0.175 with budesonide maintenance (relative rate 1.12, 0.70 to 1.79). Severe exacerbations: 9 with budesonide-formoterol against 23 with albuterol (relative risk 0.40, 0.18 to 0.86) and 21 with budesonide maintenance. Mean inhaled budesonide was 107 µg/day with as-needed budesonide-formoterol and 222 µg/day with maintenance.
